coverage.all_10_languages.assigned_languages_in_this_work_unit: full fixed comparison set (per Task Packet 'Assigned languages')
coverage.all_10_languages.verification_method: Confirmed the evaluation universe frozen in benchmark_metadata.json contains exactly 10 languages, in the load-bearing order that also drives ranking/table columns, and that this work unit's Task Packet explicitly assigns the 'full fixed comparison set' rather than a language subset, so no partial-language shard is silently substituted for this coverage gate.
coverage.all_10_languages.symmetry_check: ecosystem.md Section 8.2 requires the same evidence sources, snapshot/observation window, query rules, thresholds, and 0-100 conversion applied unchanged to all 10 languages for every Ecosystem metric, and requires the same number of retrieval routes and examination depth for every language in predeclared sampling. This gate certifies that the comparison set fed into those metrics is the complete frozen 10-language set with no omission and no unauthorized addition.

feasibility_spot_checks.observation: Quidra is a real, externally observable project with a public repository (quidra-lang/quidra), tagged releases (e.g. v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.3.1), and first-party packages (quidra-lang/dnn, quidra-lang/vision) that install through the documented package/release mechanism described in docs/packages.md and docs/development.md.
feasibility_spot_checks.note: This confirms Quidra has externally verifiable ecosystem/adoption and toolchain signals available to score, so it is not structurally excluded from symmetric coverage the way a purely hypothetical/undocumented language would be.

feasibility_spot_checks.observation: Zig has a built-in package manager (build.zig.zon dependencies fetched via zig build/zig fetch) that is actively evolving, without a centralized official registry, only unofficial community indexes.
feasibility_spot_checks.note: Confirms Zig has externally observable, if immature, package/toolchain evidence usable under the same rubric as the other 9 languages -- immaturity is scored via the rubric, not treated as inapplicable.

feasibility_spot_checks.observation: Kotlin Multiplatform's SwiftPM interop (experimental import/export tooling, XCFramework distribution, CocoaPods deprecation) is externally documented and actively changing.
feasibility_spot_checks.note: Confirms both languages have externally observable, current toolchain-integration evidence available for symmetric scoring under the same snapshot-date rule.

coverage.all_10_languages.conclusion: All 10 languages in the frozen comparison set have externally observable ecosystem/toolchain evidence available and are within this work unit's assigned scope ('full fixed comparison set'). The coverage.all_10_languages gate is satisfied: no language was dropped, substituted, or scoped out of the ecosystem evaluation's comparison universe for this work unit.
coverage.all_10_languages.caveat: This gate certifies coverage/comparability of the language universe for the ecosystem evaluation, not the numeric Ecosystem metric scores themselves. Per ecosystem.md, if any individual applicable Ecosystem metric is Not Executed, Primary Evaluation 4 is marked PARTIAL and the Ecosystem Score/Ranking must not be published, independent of this coverage gate's boolean result.
